fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 supplies neither the condensers Φ_i nor a rank-to-Hamming-support theorem. Rank condensers preserve nonzeroness or rank, not a larger Hamming cost for every rank≥2 mixed matrix; without a frozen linear map, “enumerate all M” permits post-hoc design and is not a discriminating experiment.

Proposal 2 has no polynomial-time voltage assignment rule proving universal YES completeness without finding a satisfying assignment. If transitions are locally linearized it re-enters the marginal/phase splice obstructions; if selected from a successful section, construction hides the NP-hard witness, so enumerating unspecified S3/A4 lifts tests no defined candidate.

Proposal 3 does not justify polynomial output or construction time: degree Θ(log n) Macaulay spaces can have n^{Θ(log n)} size, Gröbner computation can be exponential, and retaining only semantically reachable normal forms may itself reveal satisfiability. Low-degree portions remain exposed to finite-difference cube relations, while degree-2–6 toys cannot discriminate the asserted asymptotic Hilbert bound.

Proposal 4 merely combines mechanisms already attacked: sparse hashes/global feature shells lose soundness, and shared selector sectors admit odd XOR/rectangle splices. No explicit protected-OR matrix or invariant prevents three cheap seed certificates from superposing, so the proposed enumeration has no frozen object to evaluate.

Proposal 5 is blocked by the proved pure-power dimension wall. Equality on the entire reachable mixed-product space requires an injective linear image of dimension at least Σ_{j≤r} binom(k,j), reaching 2^k−1; small ABP width of individual products does not reduce their linear span, and injectivity alone would not preserve Hamming weight.

Proposal 6 gives no room for multiplicative separation: arbitrary matchings already require interpolation complexity linear in q, while nearby odd covers can change pole degree or disagreements only additively. Binary simplex expansion applies essentially a common symbol-weight multiplier, and the witness/disagreement matrix and weights are unspecified, so q=3,4 fitting cannot test a defined scalable claim.
evidence: Exact verifiers for formula-oblivious sparse hashes, global pair features, generator-type punctures, sampled product folds, and modular-Kronecker folds all reduced or destroyed the finite NO/YES gap. These are finite failures, not universal no-go theorems, but proposals 1 and 4 state no mutation escaping their operative cancellation failure.

The phase/selector campaign already found gauge trivialization under universal local completeness and a weight-9 rectangle splice for a shared controlled branch. Proposal 2 lies formally outside only through an unspecified global voltage rule, not through a demonstrated construction.

The exact weighted-product campaign proved dim P_r(D)=Σ_{j≤min(k,r)} binom(k,j), and function-type merging attained the maximal exact quotient without escaping it. This directly defeats proposal 5's preservation-on-the-entire-space premise asymptotically.

Variable pair-projection witnesses were exactly tested with signed coefficients and yielded only squared norms 12 versus 14; global feature shells achieved at best 14/12. The prior RS shell also assigned perfect matchings and hard odd covers the same constant coverage polynomial, supporting the baseline objection to proposal 6.

No verifier evidence accompanies any of the six proposals, and proposals 1, 2, 4, and 6 omit the explicit matrices needed for exact all-mixed-word enumeration. The suggested finite tests therefore cannot presently produce reproducible pass/fail outcomes.
next_experiment: None. Reopen only as a new candidate after supplying a frozen polynomial-time explicit matrix plus an a priori all-mixed-word invariant; for a rank-condensing mutation, preregister Φ and require exact q=3 enumeration to retain NO distance strictly above worst YES distance while improving the unfurled rank exponent across relabelings.
